description: Somos un equipo de la Escuela Técnica Austral de Petroleros Jerárquicos de Caleta Olivia, Argentina, apasionados por la ciencia, la tecnología y el espacio. Empleamos IA para seguir aprendiendo a programar, hardware y software libre para desarrollar proyectos y resolver problemas reales en equipo. Con nuestra pasión, curiosidad e innovación, queremos aportar creatividad y soluciones desde la Patagonia a un mundo cada vez más interconectado en el NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. ¡Muchas gracias!
summary:
Hello! We are the Supernova-ETA26 team.
We research how to improve agricultural production through technology and artificial intelligence.
Our challenge is titled "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data." To address it, we created GROWVIA, an intelligent platform designed for agricultural producers in Los Antiguos, Perito Moreno, Pampa Ondulada, and Gobernador Gregores.
We have developed a smart-farming web platform that guides farmers across various Argentine regions in deciding what to grow and when. The future is also something that is cultivated.
details:
Growvia is an intelligent platform that helps agricultural producers in Los Antiguos, Perito Moreno, Gobernador Gregores, and Pampa Ondulada make better decisions regarding their crops and soil management. It combines NASA satellite observations—such as climate data, soil information, and specific crop characteristics—to recommend crop rotations tailored to each individual farm.

Our goal is to transform complex satellite data into simple, practical, and intuitive tools for those who work the land, helping them improve soil health and adapt to changing conditions.

What problem are we trying to solve?

Producers face growing challenges, including:

  • Temperature and climate shifts.
  • Droughts and limited water availability.
  • Difficulties in choosing what to grow and how to plan crop rotations.
  • Often, producers lack the necessary information to plan ahead. Growvia integrates scientific and local data into a single, unified tool.

What exactly does Growvia do?

  • Farm registration: Producers register their land—including its name, location, production system, and irrigation method—to access a dashboard containing data specific to their site.
  • Crop rotation recommendations: Growvia compares various potential crop rotations against the current one. It identifies the most suitable options and evaluates their effectiveness, providing a score that explains how—and why—each aspect (soil, water, climate, and economics) is improved.
  • Interactive satellite map: This feature includes layers for vegetation (NDVI and EVI), soil temperature, snow cover, salinity risk, topography, and weather forecasts. Hovering the cursor over the map reveals precise values ​​for specific points, such as temperature (e.g., 25.1°C) or vegetation indices.
  • Climate and risk assessment: The platform provides 20 years of daily NASA climate data, weather forecasts, frost calendars, wind and snow data for the watershed, and information on the El Niño/La Niña phenomena, complete with contingency planning. Soil analysis: texture, organic matter, pH, water-holding capacity, and a soil health index—with a comprehensive assessment for each site.
  • Report: a complete plan, including recommended crop rotations and their projected effectiveness, available for printing or sharing.

Growwy, the new Intelligent System (IS)

Growwy is Growvia’s assistant, represented by the figure of "Pachamama"—Mother Earth in Andean tradition—as a symbol of soil stewardship. Growwy:

  • reads crop-related data (climate, soil, vegetation, and rotation) and answers questions in plain, simple language;
  • explains recommendations and suggests specific actions to take at any given time;
  • includes a built-in voice assistant.

What are the benefits?

  • Water savings and improved management: helps plan irrigation based on soil and climate conditions.
  • Soil protection: promotes crop rotations that enhance fertility, reduce erosion, and preserve organic matter.
  • Climate risk prevention: enables anticipation of frosts, droughts, and strong winds.
  • Better economic decision-making: compares alternatives based on costs, potential revenue, and required labor.
  • Accessibility:
    • voice-based interaction with Growwy;
    • offline functionality using the most recently saved data;
    • shareable reports;
    • available in both Spanish and English;
    • accessible via web, desktop application (Windows, Mac, and Linux), and mobile app (Android), with automatic updates.
    • Open data: all sources used are public and freely accessible.

What are our goals?

We aim to help producers in Los Antiguos and other regions make informed decisions using up-to-date data, care for their soil, optimize water use, and prepare for climate-related contingencies. We want to provide a tool that brings together technology and data to serve farmers.

What tools, languages, hardware, or software do we use?

  • TypeScript: for logic, agronomic calculations, and data processing. JavaScript / React and Next.js: the web platform and its interactivity.
  • CSS (Tailwind): visual design, light and dark modes.
  • MapLibre: interactive satellite map.
  • Rust (Tauri): desktop and Android applications with automatic updates.
  • GitHub and GitHub Actions: code, build process, and release publishing.
  • Vercel: web platform deployment.
  • VS Code: development environment.
  • Google Docs: documentation and organization.
  • Use of artificial intelligence:
  • Gemini: data analysis and problem-solving.
  • ChatGPT: organization and development of the proposal.
  • Knowunity: learning support.
  • Claude: development of project logic and structure.
  • EcoGPT: environmental and sustainability focus.

Data used:

From NASA:

  • NASA POWER: 20 years of daily climate data (temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity, UV radiation).
  • NASA GIBS: daily satellite imagery for the map.
  • MODIS MOD13Q1 (NDVI and EVI): vegetation indices (16-day intervals, 250m resolution).
  • MODIS: surface temperature and snow cover.
  • SMAP: soil moisture, used to estimate salinity risk.

Other open sources:

  • Open-Meteo: weather forecasting.
  • Copernicus Sentinel-2: true-color satellite imagery of the farm.
  • SoilGrids 250m (ISRIC): global soil map.
  • Oceanic Niño Index (NOAA): El Niño / La Niña.
  • Terrain Tiles: terrain relief and elevation.
  • OpenStreetMap: street map and location search.
  • FAO-56: international method for calculating crop water requirements.
